title: fix(gpu): headless compute seam with probe, CPU fallback and a parity-tested binning kernel
body:
## What changed

- A new crate `crates/gpu` (`camcraft-gpu`) holds the headless GPU compute seam.
  - `adapter.rs`: the windowless device policy. The software adapter comes first, then the hardware adapter (#615). This code moved down from `camcraft-ui`'s `headless_gpu.rs`.
  - `probe.rs`: the capability probe. It reads `DownlevelFlags::COMPUTE_SHADERS` and the device limits. A WebGL2 or GL adapter below ES 3.1 gives "no compute" by name.
  - `shared.rs`: one device for each process (`OnceLock`). The first request makes it. A device-lost callback marks it lost. After that, the CPU path runs for the rest of the process.
  - `switch.rs`: `CAMCRAFT_GPU_COMPUTE=off` (also `0`, `false`, `no`) turns GPU compute off. The fallback reason is logged one time for each process.
  - `binning.rs`, `binning_gpu.rs`, `binning.wgsl`: the first kernel, conservative facet binning. The input is facet boxes in tile-relative f32, padded by `r` and a margin. The output is one facet list for each cell.
- Each entry returns `Result`. An `Err` names the reason: no adapter, no compute, the switch is off, a lost device, a buffer past the limit, or a failed kernel or read-back. The caller then runs its CPU grid. There is no `unwrap` on a GPU future.
- Both binning paths check a 256 MiB host memory budget before they allocate cell lists. The check includes empty input.
- Host list, upload and read-back allocations use fallible reservation. The CPU twin returns `Result`.
- GPU error scopes capture validation, internal and out-of-memory errors through submission and read-back. Each scope is popped before return.
- `camcraft-ui`: `headless_gpu.rs` now re-exports the moved policy. No call site changed.
- `camcraft-motion`: a lib test writes and checks the recorded grid fixture (`crates/gpu/tests/fixtures/facet_grid_2619.grid`). Motion gets no GPU dependency.
- `xtask`: `ALL_CRATES`, `BATCH_CRATES` and `CLIPPY` name `gpu`. The gate tests that count crates and follow the crate reach now include `gpu`. The batch prebuild fixture writes the `gpu` crate.
- The root `Cargo.toml` adds `wgpu = "=30.0.1"`. This is a new direct dependency. It is the same version that `egui-wgpu` 0.36.2 already locks. `Cargo.lock` adds only the `camcraft-gpu` entry, so the lock still has one wgpu.
- The decision entry is `docs/decisions/2620-gpu-compute-seam.md`. It covers the new crate edge `camcraft-ui -> camcraft-gpu`, the wgpu pin, and the dropped options.

The reviewer must set `needs-maintainer`: this PR adds a new direct dependency (`wgpu`).

## Cause

The generators run in `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-motion`, and in the CLI and MCP with no window. They had no GPU access. Only `camcraft-ui` linked wgpu, and the headless device policy was in the UI crate. This PR is slice 2 of #2526. It is part of the fix of #3336 (the stock simulation is slow because it does not use the GPU).

## Tests

- `camcraft-gpu` `bin_parity`:
  - `twin_bins_hold_every_f64_grid_entry`: the CPU twin of the kernel holds each f64 entry of the recorded #2619 grid.
  - `gpu_bins_hold_every_f64_grid_entry_when_an_adapter_exists`: the GPU result holds each f64 entry. Without an adapter, the test prints a loud SKIP. `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1` makes the skip fail.
  - `twin_and_gpu_bins_hold_the_f64_cells_of_off_border_boxes` (new on this head): 200 boxes with edges inside cells, on a far origin.
- `camcraft-gpu` `refusals`: non-finite boxes and specs, a plan past the device limits, an empty set, no compute, and the off switch. Each gives an `Err` with the reason.
- `camcraft-gpu` unit tests: the probe (WebGL2, a missing compute flag, zero workgroup storage, default limits) and the switch values.
- The host memory pins are `host_budget_refuses_large_empty_and_nonempty_grids_before_allocation` and `twin_host_budget_counts_lists_and_offsets_together`.
- `gpu_failures_name_the_error_class_for_cpu_fallback` pins the named conversion for all three GPU error classes.
- `camcraft-motion` `gpu_parity_fixture_matches_the_grid`: the recorded fixture matches the f64 grid byte for byte.
- The repaired GPU path ran on the software adapter `llvmpipe (LLVM 21.1.8, 256 bits)` via Vulkan: 4349 f64 entries, 4921 binned. Earlier runs used Metal on Apple M3 Max and WARP on Windows.
- Red before the fix: not applicable. This is a new crate, so the tests cannot run on unchanged code. The mutations below show that the pins catch errors.

Mutation results (each mutation was restored after the run):

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `binning.wgsl`: inner loop `cx <= x1` changed to `cx < x1` | red: `GPU: facet 0 missing from cell 41` |
| `binning.wgsl`: `cell` gives `floor(v / s) + 1.0` | red: `GPU (off border): facet 68 missing from cell 4` |
| `binning.rs`: `cell32` gives `floor + 1.0` | red: `CPU twin (off border): facet 68 missing from cell 4`. The recorded fixture alone stayed green, so the off-border test was added. |
| `switch.rs`: only `"0"` turns compute off | red: `off_values_turn_compute_off_by_name` |
| Remove `plan`'s `host_layout` check | RED: `host_budget_refuses_large_empty_and_nonempty_grids_before_allocation`; restored GREEN. |
| Remove the CPU twin's `host_layout` check | RED: `twin_host_budget_counts_lists_and_offsets_together`; restored GREEN. |
| Convert `OutOfMemory` to the validation error name | RED: `gpu_failures_name_the_error_class_for_cpu_fallback`; restored GREEN. |

The f32 margin in `pad_boxes` has no red mutation. A margin error shows only at a cell border with a rounding error, and the fixture coordinates are exact in f32.

## Gate

Final head: `ea26996f03fc9fb0255cbe339170b90300417dbf`.

- `cargo test -p camcraft-gpu`: GREEN, 15 tests. The GPU parity path ran through Vulkan on the software adapter named above.
- Base: `upstream/main` at `62353ac753947eba162538e0d9305ad86858cfb3`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on `17c829274d574b9174e242cba99ae67ac933e853`: 1083 of 1084 steps GREEN, 53.2 minutes. Only clippy failed, on the new `chunks_exact_mut` call.
- The final head uses `as_chunks_mut::<4>()`. `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --failed gate-logs/quick-20261122-111940` passed the failed step: 1 of 1 GREEN, 47 seconds. The other 1083 results are from the prior head. A full quick sweep did not run again on the final head.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: GREEN on the final head: 258 of 258 steps, 0 failed, 49.3 minutes. The kernel, motion and app lanes passed. Four known-fail probes matched their expected failures (three for #1950 and one for #2849).
- Gate clippy on `camcraft-gpu`, `camcraft-motion` and `camcraft-ui`: GREEN after the correction.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-gpu -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-ui -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: RED. The unchanged `xtask/src/unit_sweep.rs:67` has `needless_bool`. The prior body already reported this lint. The gate's clippy step does not include `xtask`.
- The three review repair mutations above gave RED results. Each restored pin gave a GREEN result.

## Goldens moved

None. No posted output changes in this slice. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changed.

## Not exercised

- A forced GPU allocation or internal failure. The conversion test injects error values; it does not exhaust device memory.
- A real device-lost event. The callback code is in `shared.rs`, but no test forces a device loss.
- A wasm32 build of the crate.
- No production caller uses the kernel yet. The wiring into the app is #2621.

## Overlaps

- #3304 (zh-CN i18n draft) changes the root `Cargo.toml` (the workspace member list and the workspace dependencies) and `crates/ui/Cargo.toml` (the dependency list). It adds different lines. Whichever PR merges second refreshes.

Process change: yes

Changelog: The new `camcraft-gpu` crate gives headless GPU compute to the CLI, MCP and tests. It has a capability probe, one cached device, the `CAMCRAFT_GPU_COMPUTE=off` switch, a CPU fallback with a logged reason, and a facet binning kernel with parity tests.

Refs #3336
Fixes #2620
